## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vaṭṭapotakacariya* (Cp 29) is a canonical verse narrative belonging to the *Cariyāpiṭaka* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [Bareau; SuttaCentral]. The poem recounts a past life of the Bodhisatta in Magadha as a young, helpless quail without developed wings, resting as a fledgling in the nest while being fed by its mother [Bareau]. The text is translated into English by Bhikkhu Sujato as *The Conduct of the Young Quail*, and has also been translated into French by André Bareau under the title *La Conduite de la Petite Caille* [Bareau; SuttaCentral].

According to SuttaCentral, this narrative corresponds to the *Vaṭṭakajātaka* (Ja 35) [SuttaCentral]. In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 21 internal Pali matches across two commentary texts: 15 matching passages with the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (reaching 0.94 similarity in segments §8.1–9.4) and 6 matching passages with the first volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (reaching 0.92 similarity across §8.1–9.4) [DharmaNexus]. These matches correspond to the traditional connection noted between the text and Ja 35 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections at a score of 10 or above [DharmaNexus].
